title: Excelsoft Technologies Ltd - 544617 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Excelsoft Q1 FY27 revenue rose 44.05% YoY to INR802.63 million, while EBITDA margin fell to 16.24% from 18.02%.
summary.overview: Revenue from operations grew 44.05% YoY to INR802.63 million, led by the education technology services (ETS) business, which grew 177% YoY. EBITDA rose 29.78% to INR130.31 million, but margin contracted about 178 bps to 16.24% due to nearshore build-out, international sales hiring, one-time recruitment and AI training costs. PAT rose 57.13% to INR92.28 million, helped by lower interest cost. Management guided FY27 revenue of INR350-360 crore and year-end EBITDA margin of 24-25%.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR7.8 million last year (per Q&A)
Management expects to normalise to last year's level or slightly lower by year-end

segments.name: Education technology services (ETS)
segments.commentary: Approximately 63.4% of Q1 revenue; grew 177% YoY, driven by large engagements and nearshore expansion. Management attributed Q4 US onsite placements to wins now showing in Q1.

segments.name: Assessment and proctoring solutions
segments.commentary: Approximately 23.5% of revenue. Management said product revenue was roughly flat YoY in Q1 and guided 25-30% product growth for the full year.

segments.name: Learning and student success; learning design services
segments.commentary: Remaining revenue share, described as stable contributors; no separate figures given.

segments.name: Nearshore operations
segments.commentary: About INR10 crore revenue in Q1 at about 26% gross margin, up from single digits at inception; nearly INR40 crore secured for FY27 and 35-40% gross margin targeted over time.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance of INR350-360 crore; management said it is confident of about INR350 crore and could stretch closer, but would not commit to INR400 crore.
FY27 EBITDA margin guided at 24-25%; management said it would rather deliver a higher top line at about 25% margin than grow 20-25% at 27-30% margin.
Management said 30%-plus revenue growth is targeted; Q1 is typically 20-22% of annual revenue.
AQA: about USD17 million revenue visibility over four years, with about INR2.5 crore booked in Q1 and INR12-15 crore billing expected in FY27; no quantified contribution in FY28.
Long-term growth mix of roughly 69-70% organic and 30% inorganic over the next five years, per management.
Product revenue expected to grow 25-30% for the full year, with Q1 seasonally low on test volumes.
capex_capacity: Fresh capitalization about INR4 crore in Q1 for AI-native products; management said investment was front-loaded and would normalise to last year's level or slightly lower by year-end.
Nearshore delivery team being built; management said it will not add nearshore capacity beyond customer necessity.
Exploring a Toronto, Canada office to place US-facing staff for business development given visa difficulties.
Three acquisition targets in pipeline: one US, two India. Non-binding offers issued for two; one earlier target in final negotiation stage, with decision expected within a couple of weeks.
Cash and FDs of about INR400 crore; management described balance sheet as healthy.
demand_pricing: Top 5 customers about 70% of Q1 revenue; top 10 about 83%.
Nearshore team now serves 2 clients, up from 1 at start.
AQA engagement (GCSE e-marking) in pilot and phased deployment; described as second-largest account once it scales.
Management pursuing National Testing Agency-related opportunity after recent exam problems; met a government 4-member task force.
Expansion in US, UK and Dubai sales teams cited as driving pipeline and new logo wins; no pricing data disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Why are margins guided at 24-25% when earlier commentary implied 30-31% for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the earlier view excluded sales hiring and internal capability costs. It chose a conservative 24-25% EBITDA target, with possible further AI-related investment, and expects faster top-line growth to offset percentage margin pressure.

qa_highlights.question: Are the one-time costs confined to FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth of 30%-plus needs investment, and further spend may be required, so it would not commit to margin recovery beyond 25%.

qa_highlights.question: Is Q1 seasonally weakest, and what is the FY27 revenue number?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 is typically 20-22% of annual revenue. Management guided INR350-360 crore, and said INR400 crore was not committed.

qa_highlights.question: How much AQA revenue is booked and what is the scale?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR2.5 crore booked in Q1 with billing started; INR12-15 crore expected in FY27. Four-year visibility is roughly USD17 million, with upside.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the acquisitions?
qa_highlights.answer: Three targets: one US and two India. Non-binding offers issued for two; one is in final negotiation stage, with outcome expected in a couple of weeks.

qa_highlights.question: Will nearshore expansion compromise margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there would be lower margins in the short term, but nearshore would be used to retain and win customers before shifting work offshore, and would not be built ahead of customer need.

qa_highlights.question: Why did PAT exceed EBIT by so much?
qa_highlights.answer: Management explained that other income sits below operating EBIT in the presentation and interest was the major item; interest was INR15.05 million vs INR7.8 million last year.

risks_watch: EBITDA margin contraction to 16.24% in Q1; FY27 guidance of 24-25% implies recovery in later quarters.
Interest expense nearly doubled to INR15.05 million YoY; watch debt and cost of funding.
High client concentration: top 5 customers 70% of revenue.
Product revenue flat YoY in Q1; 25-30% full-year growth requires a pick-up in test volumes.
Acquisition execution risk; one deal previously written off and renegotiated.
Ongoing AI upskilling spend may continue for about two years, per management.
AQA ramp depends on phased deployment; no FY28 contribution quantified.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth and pipeline, but cautious and conservative on margins: management repeatedly chose to guide to 24-25% EBITDA and said it would 'deliver more probably.' Answers on acquisitions, AQA and the Q&A on product growth were sometimes vague or unquantified.
key_quotes: We would want to take the first one, right? So, grow at a faster pace, so that we acquire the market quickly, and then grow to a, God forbid, let's say, God willing, a INR1,000 crores company earlier than anybody's normal imagination.
So we are in that direction and we are pretty much confident on achieving those numbers.

Doreswamy Palaniswamy: Sir, we would be, as we have kind of in the last quarter also we mentioned that we would be somewhere around like 24%, 25% on our margin, that's going to be the year end margin.
And that is a training that will go on, up-skilling that will go on for a couple of more years.
So we want to do is ensure that it would be a 25% for sure.
Excluding these one -time expenses, our operating margins remain broadly stable year -over-year, demonstrating the resilience of our core operating model.

adds.what: Nearshore delivery team being built (no capacity count given; management will not add beyond customer necessity)

growth.why: FY27 revenue guided at INR350-360 crore (new) with confidence in about INR350 crore, backed by nearshore (nearly INR40 crore secured for FY27), AQA billing of INR12-15 crore and product growth 25-30%; however EBITDA margin guide of 24-25% is a cut from ~30% previously expected, and no specific capacity additions are quantified.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guided FY27 EBITDA margin of 24-25% from a 16.24% Q1 base, which requires a steep recovery, and nearshore gross margin is about 26% today versus a 35-40% target over time.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Nearshore delivery team is being built for 2 clients (up from 1), with nearly INR40 crore secured for FY27, but management will not add nearshore capacity beyond customer necessity and no capacity count is given.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: ETS revenue grew 177% YoY to about 63.4% of Q1 revenue, product growth is guided at 25-30% for FY27 (Q1 product revenue roughly flat), and management targets 30%-plus revenue growth.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex is not discussed as a formal programme; fresh capitalisation is about INR4 crore in Q1 for AI-native products, expected to normalise to last year's level or slightly lower by year-end, and the Toronto office and acquisitions are still at exploration or negotiation stage, so no firm capex plan is in place.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management said it is confident of about INR350 crore and could stretch closer to the INR360 crore top end, but would not commit to INR400 crore; Q1 revenue grew 44.05% YoY to INR802.63 million.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q1 EBITDA margin fell to 16.24% from 18.02%, and FY27 guidance needs a recovery to 24-25%; management said further AI-related spend may be needed and interest cost nearly doubled to INR15.05 million, so the margin path carries execution risk even though revenue guidance is held at INR350-360 crore.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: AQA (GCSE e-marking) is in pilot and phased deployment with about INR2.5 crore booked in Q1 and INR12-15 crore billing expected in FY27; AI-native products are receiving investment.

rows.label: AQA contract ramp to INR12-15 crore FY27 billing
rows.why: About USD17 million over four years of visibility with INR2.5 crore booked in Q1 and INR12-15 crore billing expected in FY27, though no FY28 contribution is quantified.

rows.label: Acquisition decision on one target
rows.when: within a couple of weeks of the call
rows.why: One earlier target is in final negotiation with a decision expected in a couple of weeks; three targets in pipeline (one US, two India) with non-binding offers issued for two.

rows.label: Interest cost nearly doubling
rows.why: Interest expense rose to INR15.05 million from INR7.8 million YoY despite a cash balance of about INR400 crore, so the cost of funding is a watch item rather than an easing trend.

tone.note: Management was confident on ETS growth (177% YoY), the pipeline and the INR350-360 crore revenue guide, but cautious and conservative on margins, choosing 24-25% EBITDA over 30%; analysts pushed on why margins were cut from the earlier 30-31% view, and answers on acquisitions, AQA and product growth
